WHY: The conflicting descriptions make the documented behavior unclear; the source rates this NIT. === END CONSENSUS FINDINGS === === CONSENSUS TASK GAPS === (No task gaps reported.) === END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS === === FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro === (No findings reported.) === END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro === === FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 === - .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:Lines 144-148 | severity=NIT | confidence=4 PROBLEM: The comment describes the repo-wide listing as "the same listing and newest-100 window the poller's `_pr_named_review_dispatch_runs` reads (issue #4701)". After issue #4927 was merged, the poller's `_pr_named_review_dispatch_runs` was rewritten in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` to issue paged per-wrapper REST listings (`actions/workflows//runs?event=workflow_dispatch&created=>=&per_page=100&page=

`, at most 10 pages per wrapper), NOT a single 100-run repo-wide page. WHY: A consumer-repo poller with a busy `workflow_dispatch` history could push a live `AI Review [pr:]` run off the 100-run window, leaving the hand-off stuck at `waiting for verified completed review run` even though the poller's `_pr_named_review_dispatch_runs` would have found it. The plan for #4927 explicitly scopes this checker out (AD-16 of the plan), so it is a documented deferral — but the inline comment now misrepresents the two callers' behaviour and will mislead the next reader. - agents.md:Lines 1064-1077 | severity=NIT | confidence=4 PROBLEM: The bullet for the verdict helper says PR-named runs are "counted from one repo-wide `workflow_dispatch` listing (newest 100 runs) read only when the head-branch reads found nothing". The text below the same bullet (lines 2077-2093) is up to date and says the helper pages per wrapper in three calls in this repo. So `agents.md` carries both the old (newest-100-page) and the new (paged-per-wrapper) descriptions in different sections of the same file. WHY: It does not — but it is a contract break in the `agents.md` doc, which §6 treats as a behaviour contract for operator-facing surfaces. The new description is the one true behaviour; the old description should be removed. - scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, `_pr_named_review_dispatch_runs`, the block that calls `printf '%s\n%s\n' "${_pnr_runs}" "${_pnr_wrapper_runs}" | jq -cs '.[0] + .[1]'` after the `for` loop HARDENING_SUGGESTION: When the listing is incomplete the function still prints a JSON array (possibly empty, possibly partial) on stdout and returns 1. Every caller checks the return code and discards the array, so this is safe — but a future caller that forgets the return-code check (or that uses `set -e` and `$(...)` substitution) could silently treat a partial array as a complete one. The function already logs `PR_NAMED_REVIEW_RUNS … outcome=incomplete` on stderr; it could also emit the empty array on stdout when incomplete. SUGGESTED_MINIMAL_FIX: Replace the final `printf '%s\n' "${_pnr_matches:-[]}"` with `if [ -n "${_pnr_reason}" ]; then printf '[]\n'; else printf '%s\n' "${_pnr_matches:-[]}"; fi`. ~3 lines. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2 - scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, `_mt_release`, the `grep -Fxq -e "pr:${num}" ${head:+-e "${head}"}` line HARDENING_SUGGESTION: `${head:+-e "${head}"}` correctly avoids the empty-pattern bug, but `${head}` itself is a head branch like `claude/issue-10`, which can contain characters that are not `regex` literals but are valid `grep -F` (fixed-string) literals. No issue today, but if a future head ref contains a literal `-e` (extremely unlikely in a Git ref but possible in a synthetic test fixture), the `${head}` expansion would be parsed as a new `-e` flag. Pin the position with `--`: `grep -Fxq -- -e "pr:${num}" ${head:+-e "${head}"} --` and place the head-branch pattern after a second `--` so it can never be read as a flag. SUGGESTED_MINIMAL_FIX: `printf '%s\n' "${inflight_review_branches}" | grep -Fxq -e "pr:${num}" ${head:+-e "${head}"}` becomes `printf '%s\n' "${inflight_review_branches}" | grep -Fxq -- -e "pr:${num}" ${head:+-e "${head}"} --`. 1 line. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1 === END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 === === FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 === (No findings reported.) === END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
